rows.name: ENABLE_FUSE_STATS

cells.Set by: Developers who build without FUSE stats.
cells.Values and default: Text for the CMake option `ENABLE_FUSE_STATS`, for example `ON` or `OFF`. The makefile passes the text without a check. `make ENABLE_FUSE_STATS=OFF` also works. Unset: `ON`. Empty: the makefile passes the empty text to CMake, and CMake counts empty text as off.
cells.Effect: Selects at CMake configure time whether FUSE stats are compiled into the programs. `GNUmakefile` passes the text to `cmake` as `-DENABLE_FUSE_STATS=<value>`. A changed value rewrites the file `gen/.fuse_stats_stamp`, and `make` then runs CMake configure again. `GNUmakefile` passes the value only for builds in `gen/` and for `make deb`. The sanitizer, coverage and `deb-host` builds do not get it. For a build on an LSF worker (`REMOTE`), a `make` command-line value and a non-empty environment value reach the worker.

rows.name: FUSE_STATS_STAMP

cells.Values and default: File path. This is an internal make variable. `GNUmakefile` assigns it and ignores an environment value, except when the only goals are `list-tests` or `list-tests-core`. Unset: `gen/.fuse_stats_stamp`. When the only goals are `list-tests` or `list-tests-core`, the text is empty.
cells.Effect: An environment value changes no build result. For the goals `list-tests` and `list-tests-core` alone, `make` puts the value into the prerequisite lists of the CMake configure targets and the package target. `make` does not build those targets for these goals. The file holds the last `ENABLE_FUSE_STATS` value. A changed file makes `make` run CMake configure again. `make FUSE_STATS_STAMP=path` on the command line replaces the path for every goal.

rows.name: HAS_AVX512

cells.Values and default: Only the text `no` has an effect. On Linux the makefile assigns `yes` or `no` itself and ignores an environment value. On macOS it uses the environment value. Unset: on Linux, `yes` when `/proc/cpuinfo` holds the text `avx512f`, otherwise `no`. On macOS, empty text.
cells.Effect: `no` means that the CPU of the build host has no AVX-512 (a CPU instruction set). `make t_<name>` then builds the test and stops with an error before the run. When `REMOTE` is `0`, `test`, `test-core`, `test-host`, `test-fpga`, `test-fast` and `test-proxy` stop with an error and build nothing. `make HAS_AVX512=value` on the command line replaces the detected value on Linux too. The `-old` test targets stop in the same way. The sanitizer and coverage targets do not check the variable.

rows.name: INGEST_PYTHON_VERSION

problems.statement: When `IN_NIX_SHELL` is set, `ingest-deps` skips `uv` and the value has no effect.
problems.code_says: The recipe tests `[ -n "$$IN_NIX_SHELL" ]`. A set but empty IN_NIX_SHELL does not skip `uv`.

cells.Set by: Nobody by default. Developers may override it.
cells.Values and default: A Python version that `uv` (the Python package tool) accepts for `--python`. The makefile does not check it. `make INGEST_PYTHON_VERSION=value` also works. Unset: the value of `TOKENIZER_PYTHON_VERSION`. `README.dependencies.md` records the pinned value. Empty: the makefile keeps the empty text, and `--python` gets no version.
cells.Effect: Selects the Python version of the two ingest environments, `ingest/export/.venv` and `ingest/runtime/.venv`. The target `ingest-deps` passes it to `uv sync --frozen --python`. When `IN_NIX_SHELL` is not empty, `ingest-deps` skips `uv` and the value has no effect. `make python-deps`, `make deb` and `make deb-host` also run `ingest-deps`.

rows.name: NPROC_BUILD

cells.Read by: `make`, the Nix build `tron-cmake-test-build`, CI workflows (`GNUmakefile`, `bin/ci/ci-select-tron-build-jobs.sh`, `nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix` and other files)
cells.Set by: CI workflows, the Nix build and `bin/bsub-build`.
cells.Values and default: Positive integer, a number of parallel jobs. `GNUmakefile` passes the text to `-j` without a check. `bin/ci/ci-select-tron-build-jobs.sh` stops with an error unless the text is digits with no leading `0`. `make NPROC_BUILD=4` also works. Unset: `GNUmakefile` uses the smaller of 16 jobs and the `nproc` output. The script stops with an error.
cells.Effect: `GNUmakefile` adds `-j <value>` to the options of `make` and to its `cmake --build` commands, except the one of the goals `iwyu` and `iwyu-check`. In the Nix build, the job count is the smaller of `NIX_BUILD_CORES` and this value. For a build on an LSF worker (`REMOTE`), `bin/bsub-build` replaces the local value with the value of `REMOTE_BUILD_CORES`. The CI workflows that set it and the Nix build set 16 jobs.

rows.name: TOKENIZER_PYTHON_VERSION

cells.Set by: CI workflow `publish-deb.yml`, on the `make` command line.

rows.name: TRON_HOME_ROOT

cells.Set by: Nothing in the repository sets it.
cells.Values and default: Path of the directory that holds the home directories. The script compares it as text with the physical path of `HOME` (symbolic links resolved). Unset: `/home`.
cells.Effect: `bin/scratch-dir.sh` creates a build directory below `TRON_SCRATCH_USERS` only when the physical path of `HOME` is below this directory and the checkout is below `HOME`. The script does not resolve symbolic links in the value. When the comparison fails, a new build directory is a plain directory in the checkout, not a link. `GNUmakefile` runs the script.

rows.name: TRON_SCRATCH_USERS

problems.statement: For each build directory, `bin/scratch-dir.sh` creates `<value>/...` and puts a symbolic link to it in the checkout.
problems.code_says: The script creates the directory only for a build directory that does not exist yet. An existing link whose target is outside the new value stays as it is, so a changed value does not move an existing build. `--remove` then deletes only the link.

cells.Set by: Nothing in the repository sets it.

cells.Effect: For each build directory, `bin/scratch-dir.sh` creates `<value>/<HOME below TRON_HOME_ROOT>/tmp/<checkout path below HOME>/<directory>` and puts a symbolic link to it in the checkout. The build directories are `gen`, `gen-deb`, `gen-deb-host`, `gen-tsan`, `gen-asan` and `gen-coverage`. A new build directory is a plain directory in the checkout, not a link, when `CI` is not empty or when `cmake` is missing or older than version 3.24. rows.name: REMOTE

cells.Set by: Developers. `bin/bsub-build` sets `0` inside the LSF job.
cells.Values and default: Exactly one of `0`, `1`, `sku0`, `sku1`. Spaces around the value are removed. Any other text stops `make` with an error. `make REMOTE=1` also works. Unset: the value of `TRON_REMOTE_EXECUTION` (default `0`) for build goals and test goals, and `0` for other goals. Empty: `make` stops with an error.
cells.Effect: `0` runs everything on the local host. `1`, `sku0` and `sku1` send the goals `all`, `build`, `core`, `build-core`, `build-prod`, `build-test`, `build-ingest`, `build-test-host` and `build-test-fpga` to an LSF worker through `bin/bsub-build`. They also add `--remote` to `bin/slice run` for `test`, `test-core`, `test-host`, `test-fpga` and `test-fast`. They stop `make` with an error for goals that run tests directly, for example `run`, `t_<name>` and `test-proxy`. `sku0` and `sku1` also add `--remote-sku=<value>` (a server class of the test pool). Other goals run on the local host.

rows.name: REMOTE_BUILD_CORES

cells.Values and default: Positive integer, a number of cores. Text with a character other than a digit, or the text `0`, stops the script with exit code 2. Unset: 16 cores.
cells.Effect: Sets the number of cores that the LSF build job reserves. The script exports the same number on the worker as `NPROC_BUILD` and `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS`. It also sets the default of `REMOTE_BUILD_MEM`, 8192 MB for each core. A `-jN` option of `make` replaces this variable with N. With a GNU make that shows `-jN` in `MAKEFLAGS` only inside recipes, N replaces it only when N differs from `NPROC_BUILD`. `README.md` names those versions. A value with a leading `0` passes the check, and the memory default reads it in base 8.

rows.name: REMOTE_BUILD_MEM

cells.Set by: Developers, before a build on an LSF worker.
cells.Values and default: A number of MB (megabytes). The script does not check the text. It passes the text to `bsub` in `rusage[mem=<value>]`. Unset: 8192 MB for each core of `REMOTE_BUILD_CORES`. That is 131072 MB for the default of 16 cores.

The script prints the number with the suffix M and README.md:519 says MB, but the repository holds no LSF configuration. The LSF configuration of the lab cluster, or the `bjobs -l` output of one build job, settles it.

INGEST_PYTHON_VERSION, TOKENIZER_PYTHON_VERSION - what `uv` does when the value is empty and `--python` gets no version. The rows say only that `--python` gets no version. One run of `uv sync --frozen --python` in a scratch project settles it.

NPROC_BUILD - what GNU make does with text after `-j` in MAKEFLAGS that is not a number. The row says only that the makefile does not check the text. One `make NPROC_BUILD=abc list-tests` run settles it. Running make in the checkout was not allowed here.
REMOTE_BUILD_CORES - which GNU make versions show `-jN` in MAKEFLAGS only inside recipes. The makefile code handles both cases. The version numbers come from README.md:521 and were not tested.
notes: 12 rows checked against commit 7eddde7895. No row contradicts the code. Unchanged (4): ENABLE_FUSE_STATS, FUSE_STATS_STAMP, PRESET_STAMP, TRON_HOME_ROOT. Changed for a fact (2): INGEST_PYTHON_VERSION (the recipe tests for a non-empty IN_NIX_SHELL, not for a set one) and TRON_SCRATCH_USERS (a changed value does not move the target of an existing link, and `make distclean` then removes only the link). Changed for house rules only (6): HAS_AVX512 (rule 9, the word for the avx512f entry of /proc/cpuinfo, and the plain-English hint on 'lacks'), NPROC_BUILD (rules 1, 5, 7 and 9), TOKENIZER_PYTHON_VERSION (rule 8), REMOTE (rule 1), REMOTE_BUILD_CORES (rules 6 and 9), REMOTE_BUILD_MEM (rule 6). Rule 8: the Python version number is removed from INGEST_PYTHON_VERSION and TOKENIZER_PYTHON_VERSION, and both rows point to `README.dependencies.md`, which records the pin at README.dependencies.md:211. Rule 1 cuts. NPROC_BUILD went from 1105 to 996 characters: the quoted error text is gone (also rule 7), the two sentences about the LSF worker are one sentence, and the IWYU exception now names the goals `iwyu` and `iwyu-check` in place of the tool name with its definition. REMOTE went from 1031 to 987 characters: the list of example goals that stop `make` lost 'the coverage goals'. No fact about parsing, the unset case, the main effect or overrides was removed. Rule 6: REMOTE_BUILD_CORES no longer cites a makefile comment. The row states what the makefile code does (GNUmakefile:206-208) and points to README.md for the GNU make versions. REMOTE_BUILD_MEM keeps the sentence that the repository holds no LSF configuration for the unit. A search for LSF_UNIT_FOR_LIMITS and lsf.conf content in the checkout found none. Hints. The developer-reader hint on the table title needs no cell change. The plain-English hint on TRON_SCRATCH_USERS is applied as two sentences without the count of cases. ENABLE_FUSE_STATS: the 'Empty:' statement rests on the CMake rule that `if(<variable>)` is false for an empty value (CMake documentation of `if`), not on repository code. FUSE_STATS_STAMP and PRESET_STAMP: an environment value is read only when the goals are list-tests or list-tests-core alone, and it changes nothing there. The rows say so. Whether these two internal make variables need rows at all is a decision for the document owner. No section 1 row is in this chunk, so there is no label doubt. Line numbers: README.md in the checkout holds 6 staged lines near its top, so the README.md lines cited here (519, 521) are lines 513 and 515 at commit 7eddde7895. All other cited files are unchanged from that commit.
